..
Issued at 1254 AM MDT Fri Sep 4 2026

For the first time in several days, the radar is clear across 
western and central Wyoming as well much of the surrounding states 
as much drier air has moved over the Cowboy state. This drier will 
stick around for a couple of days, but this leads to other concerns. 

We had critical fire weather across the area yesterday with the low 
humidity and gusty afternoon wind. And, it looks like we will have 
another bout of critical fire weather today. There will be roughly 
the same set up as yesterday. We continue to be between an upper 
level low over the Pacific Northwest and a ridge across the 
southeastern United States. We continue to have 20 to 30 knots of 
wind at 700 millibars along with a decent height and pressure 
gradient across the area. The NBM ensemble has at least a 3 out of 5 
chance of wind gusts over 25 mph across a good portion of the area 
this afternoon. The limiting factor today will be humidity. Somewhat 
higher humidity will move into southern Wyoming, and this should 
keep most of that area from reaching the 3 hours of critical fire 
weather to justify a Red Flag Warning. With a greater than 3 out of 
4 chance of relative humidity falling under 15 percent this 
afternoon across areas East of the Divide, we will keep the Red Flag 
Warning as is this morning. The wind may not be quite as strong in 
northern areas, but will be close enough the justify keeping the 
warning. It will be a warm day as we head into Labor Day weekend as 
well. Much of the Bighorn Basin, Wind River Basin and areas along 
and east of Interstate 25 have at least a 1 in 2 chance of reaching 
or exceeding 90 degrees today.

The ridge will retrograde over the weekend, pushing into the 
southern Plains states during the three day weekend. Temperatures 
will remain well above normal on Saturday and Sunday, with the heat 
peaking on Saturday. Most locations below 5000 feet in elevation 
will have at least a 1 in 2 chance of high temperatures of 90 or 
higher. As for fire weather, concerns should begin to ease somewhat. 
Humidity will begin to climb as another surge of monsoonal moisture 
slowly makes it's way toward the area. The core of it should remain 
east of the area on Saturday, so almost all areas should see no rain 
(the highest chance of a shower or storm is only 1 out of 10). There 
will also be less wind. Elevated fire weather conditions are still 
possible but the chance of critical fire weather looks smaller than 
today. So, we will not extend the Red Flag Warning at this time. 

The monsoonal plume will move over the area on Sunday, as the ridge 
continues to drift westward. Wyoming looks to be in a decent spot 
for the moisture, with a moist conveyor belt between the ridge and 
the upper level low that continues to spin over Oregon. A bit of 
added moisture will also be coming in from Tropical Storm Marie. 
Precipitable water values look to peak on Sunday evening, with some 
models rising to over an inch, which is close to 200 percent of 
normal. The models do sometimes overcook this though, so reality is 
probably around 20 percent less. Nevertheless, it is high for early 
September. There could be a good coverage of showers and storms 
though. The moisture will be moving in ahead of an approaching 
Pacific Cold Front and negatively tilted trough associated with the 
upper level low that will be lifting northward over Idaho. As for 
the potential of heavy rain, there is some. A mitigating factor to 
possible flooding will be that there will be steering flow, which 
will keep the storms moving. This still looks like the best chance 
for rain. It will be one more very warm day on Sunday, although more 
cloud cover could keep high temperatures a couple of degrees cooler.

The end of the holiday weekend on Labor Day will be a cooler day 
with temperatures close to seasonal averages. Drier air will likely 
be moving into the area. However, there will may be enough moisture 
wrapping around the low as it moves into Canada to bring a few 
showers and storms (a 1 in 5 to a 1 in 2 chance), mainly to northern 
and western Wyoming. With a decent pressure gradient across the 
area, it also looks like a rather breezy day, but cooler 
temperatures should keep any fire weather concerns below critical.

There is good model agreement in drier air moving over the area for 
Tuesday and Wednesday, bring a couple of nice late summer / early 
autumn days (depending on they are astronomical or meteorological 
seasons) with comfortably warm temperatures. Monsoonal moisture 
should then return for later in the week, although there are 
differences in model guidance in regards to exact timing to when it 
will arrive. So, it looks like a hot start to the holiday weekend, 
with a return to more seasonably weather for early next week. And, 
has been the case over the past couple of months, the everlasting 
monsoon will make a couple more appearances.
